transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Files shared: drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/gamma-pilot-metrics, redwood://playbook/gamma-batching-v3 (note: placeholder)

Summary:
Quick checkpoint on throughput numbers from last 48h of pilot traffic. Focus on continuous batching effectiveness, concurrency target tradeoffs, and queue shaping/backpressure. Agreed to run short A/B on concurrency 8 vs 12 and for Redwood to deliver updated batching config and playback guidance.

Topics covered:
- 48h throughput summary and KV cache hit-rate impact
- Queue depth and latency buckets (p50/p95/p99)
- Continuous batching tuning and batch size ceilings
- Concurrency targets, CPU/GPU observed saturation, and fallback policies
- Next steps and action owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this short, 45ish minutes, quick review of the numbers you cut over last night. lina you on?
[00:12] Lina (Customer): yup hi thanks, i pulled the dashboard earlier, so we have the 48 hour ingest and i flagged the p99 spikes around the 02:00 UTC window.
[00:22] Ethan (SE): yep i saw those, marco did you see any infra flaps? i didn't notice pod restarts in the logs.
[00:29] Marco (Infra): no restarts, but we had a brief cpu throttle on the autoscale group, might be noisy neighbors on the host, but GPU utilization was solid 78-84% during peak.
[00:39] Maya: perfect, so the headline: through continuous batching we pushed effective tokens/sec up ~2.6x compared to baseline, average batch size increased from ~5 to ~18, but p99 latency is up 220 ms in the worst buckets.
[00:55] Sophie (Product): is that 220ms absolute or added? what's baseline p99?
[01:02] Ethan: baseline p99 was ~420ms, so worst-case is now ~640ms — still within your 800ms SLO that you mentioned in discovery, but it's a tradeoff.
[01:12] Lina: okay that feels acceptable, but those 02:00 spikes lined up with a traffic pattern that has a lot of long-form responses, which increases kv cache churn.
[01:22] Ethan: good call — kv cache hit-rate went from ~68% down to 53% during the long response spike. with lower hit-rate you get more full decode steps per request which increases per-token cost and latency.
[01:33] Marco: we can try warming the cache for the heavy endpoints, but that adds complexity to the pipeline.
[01:38] Maya: okay, let's map the tuning knobs: continuous batching window, max batch size cap, concurrency limit, and queue depth/backpressure threshold. we recommended earlier a concurrency target of 12 for steady traffic — do we want to keep that?
[01:51] Lina: we actually ran a jitter test at 12 and 16 overnight — 16 resulted in lower CPU headroom and slight variance in p50 with weird long tails. 12 looked stable but cost was a little higher per token.
[02:03] Ethan: note: cost per token scales not just with concurrency but with batching efficiency. at 12 concurrency we saw higher average batch size which amortizes kernel overhead; at 8 concurrency batch sizes drop and unit cost rises. so it's not linear.
[02:17] Sophie: can you remind me what the observed token-cost delta was between 8 and 12?
[02:21] Ethan: rough numbers from the test: 8 concurrency — unit cost baseline 1.0x, 12 concurrency — 0.78x, 16 concurrency — 0.76x but marginal improvements after 12 were small and latency tail risk increases.
[02:36] Lina: that's useful. we care about p95/p99 more than absolute cost, but we have a cost budget. so maybe run A/B for a week but during non-peak hours?
[02:45] Maya: agreed — action: run 24h A/B of 8 vs 12 during low-traffic window, capture token-cost, p95/p99, and KV hit-rate.
[02:54] Marco: on the queueing side, we set queue depth max to 1200 by default; during the bursts we saw queue depth climb to 980 which is close to the cap — when it hits the cap we fall back to model-smaller fallback and that path had a 1.2x latency overhead and 0.6x cost improvement.
[03:13] Ethan: that's the intended graceful degradation. one idea we flagged: dynamic queue shaping — briefly reduce the max batch window when queue depth crosses 600 to prioritize latency. that reduces p99 at the expense of some batching efficiency.
[03:27] Lina: any heuristics for when to switch? like p95 > 400ms? queue depth > 600?
[03:33] Ethan: we recommend queue depth > 600 OR p95 > 350ms for your workload based on the replay we ran. those thresholds cut p99 significantly in our simulations.
[03:43] Marco: implemented that threshold in staging but need the tuned values from redwood for the batch window and cap.
[03:49] Maya: yep ethan will share the config. also note we saw a KV cache prefill script helps — warms first tokens for common prompts. it raised hit-rate by ~8 percentage points in the last run.
[04:02] Sophie: is prefill safe from a data residency perspective? we don't want to push user data into shared caches.
[04:08] Ethan: good flag — prefill only uses template prompts and not PII. also we can use customer-scoped caches in dedicated / private modes which meets your compliance needs.
[04:19] Lina: speaking of which, we may move to dedicated if the pilot meets throughput targets — timeline unknown but target decision by end of April.
[04:27] Maya: understood. if you go dedicated we can provide dedicated cache and stricter KMS integrations.
[04:33] Marco: i have a perf question: on the GPU side we saw steady utilization but host memory was creeping up — are we safe with current quantization profile?
[04:41] Ethan: we're using q4_0 quant for this trial — it yields lower memory but slightly higher per-token compute overhead relative to q4_1. we can try a hybrid: q4_0 for smaller models, q4_1 for larger—there's a tradeoff.
[04:55] Lina: will that materially change latency?
[04:58] Ethan: small shifts, in tens of milliseconds per request, not orders of magnitude. main driver is batch size and cache hit-rate.
[05:06] Maya: okay let's pivot to concrete next steps — we've already called 3 action owners. ethan, can you summarize what you'll deliver?
[05:13] Ethan: sure — i'll send a tuned continuous-batching config (json) with: max_batch_size: 20, batching_window_ms: 28, dynamic_window_lower: 12, queue_shaping_threshold: 600, fallback_model: 'x-small-v2' and an expected cost delta estimate and a playbook for ramping those changes safely.
[05:33] Maya: perfect. marco — can you confirm you'll run the 8 vs 12 concurrency test and upload the telemetry?
[05:38] Marco: yes we'll run it in staging next low-traffic window, scaffold the test with traffic-replay and export the CSVs.
[05:45] Lina: and i'll own the decision runway — if numbers look good we'll request a dedicated capacity quote.
[05:51] Sophie: quick clarifying Q: what's the plan for monitoring regressions when we flip config? any automated evals?
[05:56] Ethan: we recommend a canary rollout: 10% traffic with strict regression checks on p95/p99 and a prompt-set eval; if any regression we auto-rollback. we'll give the eval harness as part of the playbook.
[06:08] Lina: sounds good, do you have sample alerts?
[06:11] Maya: yes we'll attach a sample alert file.
[06:15] Marco: one more infra nit: when fallback engages the downstream connectors see a slightly different response envelope — our parsers are tolerant but wanted to flag it.
[06:24] Ethan: noted, we'll add a compatibility test in the playbook and include the schema diff.
[06:29] Maya: excellent. any competitor concerns? lina earlier you mentioned alternative vendors.
[06:35] Lina: we looked at Anthropic and AWS managed endpoints. Anthropic's latency looked good for short responses but cost was higher; aws sagemaker is an okay managed path but we'd lose some of the batching optimizations you provide.
[06:47] Maya: good context. last thing — pricing for burst capacity and fallback model toggles, i'll send an appendix.
[06:54] Sophie: and can you include a rough estimate for a dedicated 3-month commit?
[06:58] Maya: yes, i'll include a templated quote.
[07:02] Ethan: ok that's it from me, i'll push configs and the playbook link to the drive by 4/7.
[07:09] Lina: thanks everyone, useful sync.

(Transcript continues with brief clarifications and confirmations, timestamps abbreviated)
[30:00] Maya: recap — A/B 8 vs 12, redwood to share batching + playbook, customer to smoke test in staging, send decision timeline if moving to dedicated.
[30:12] Marco: confirmed.
[30:20] Ethan: i'll also attach a small script to inject prefill tokens safely.
[30:27] Sophie: thanks, bye.
[30:30] Lina: bye.

Meeting close.
